sources.title: Supply Contract
sources.text:
SUPPLY CONTRACT (fictional)

7. Delivery
7.2 The Supplier shall deliver the Goods within ten (10) Business Days of each order.

9. Liability
9.1 The Supplier shall not be liable for any indirect or consequential loss.

15. Termination
15.3 Either party may terminate this Contract on ninety (90) days' written notice.

citing.title: Skeleton argument
citing.text:
SKELETON ARGUMENT FOR THE CLAIMANT (fictional)

1. The contract
1.1 Under clause 15.3 of the Supply Contract, either party may terminate on notice.
1.2 Clause 9.1 of the Supply Contract says that "The Supplier shall not be liable for any indirect loss."
1.3 The Defendant also relies on clause 21.4 of the Supply Contract, which does not help it.

2. Procedure
2.1 The application is made under CPR r. 3.4(2)(a) and, in the alternative, CPR Part 24.
2.2 The Defendant cites CPR Part 112, which does not exist.

3. Authorities
3.1 See [2021] EWCA Civ 1405 and [2015] UKSC 36; and Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Exch 341.
3.2 The Defendant's reliance on [2007] UKSC 12 is misplaced.

expect.text: shall not be liable for any indirect loss

citing.text:
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF MOTION TO DISMISS (fictional)

1. Introduction
1.1 Defendant moves under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6).

2. Standard
2.1 Expert evidence is governed by Fed. R. Evid. 702. Venue may be transferred under 28 U.S.C. § 1404(a).
2.2 See Barlow v. Teague Freight, 621 F.3d 77 (2d Cir. 2010). Plaintiff cites Pell v. Ormond, 88 F.4th 501 (3d Cir. 2031) and Fed. R. App. P. 52.

3. Argument
3.1 As Section 2 explains, the standard is not met. Section 9 below addresses damages.
